selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer tracks workouts and has low price sensitivity, matching the premium pricing tier and activewear category of the brand. She responds to science-backed claims and ingredient transparency, which aligns well with messaging around recycled ocean plastic and sustainability.

The Gen Z Aesthete is highly visual and cares about whether a brand stands for something, which connects directly to the advertiser's core values of sustainability and being made from recycled ocean plastic.

The Sustainability Buyer specifically researches supply chains and will pay more for genuinely sustainable options, making them a direct fit for a brand whose primary value and material sourcing focus is sustainability and recycled ocean plastic.
The Fitness Enthusiast works out 4+ times a week and buys performance apparel, which maps directly to the activewear category and the premium tier sitting between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent loves subscriptions, whereas the advertiser's business model is explicitly a one-off purchase.
The Pet Parent focuses entirely on pet-related categories like pet food and pet health, which has no overlap with women's activewear.
The Affluent Classic prefers classic apparel and heritage messaging and is explicitly disinterested in influencer positioning and trendy language, making her a poor fit for a modern activewear brand.
The Convenience-First Millennial focuses on instant delivery and quick commerce, which does not align with a specialized D2C apparel brand.
The Value-Conscious Shopper has high price sensitivity and responds to discount-forward messaging, which conflicts with the brand's premium price tier.
The Gifter is explicitly disinterested in self-care-only framing and relies heavily on gifting occasions, whereas activewear is typically purchased for personal use.
